talks.title: #RomHack2022 - James Forshaw - The Vendor / Researcher Relationship Needs Improvement
talks.teaser: Investigates #RomHack2022 - James Forshaw - The Vendor / Researcher Relationship Needs Improvement and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Researcher–Vendor Tension

James Forshaw of Google Project Zero delivers a RomHack keynote on improving relationships between security researchers and vendors. Having reported countless Microsoft flaws while also shipping Chrome and Windows sandbox code, he sees both sides' frustrations—vendors feeling attacked, researchers feeling stonewalled.

Vendor Responsibilities

Secure products require planning for external scrutiny from day one. Forshaw warns against intentionally hindering research, arguing any widely deployed software will attract probing and organizations should design for fixability rather than obscurity—sometimes favoring memory-safe languages to reduce bug classes.

Researcher Responsibilities

Researchers face time constraints and should choose targets wisely, accepting that some issues fall outside vendor support boundaries. He cites Microsoft's policy distinguishing user-to-kernel escalation (in scope) from administrator-to-kernel paths sometimes deemed out of scope—setting expectations before investing effort.

Disclosure in Practice

Forshaw critiques clunky vendor portals but praises responsive email channels when they work. Better mutual respect, he concludes, yields more secure products—the shared goal both sides claim despite recurring friction.

talks.title: #RomHack2022 - Nestori Syynimaa - Attacking AAD abusing Synch API: The story behind 40k$ bounties
talks.teaser: Demonstrates #RomHack2022 - Nestori Syynimaa - Attacking AAD abusing Synch API: The story behind 40k$ bounties and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
AAD Connect sync basics

Nestori Syynimaa (creator of AADInternals, also referenced in APT29/Nobelium reporting) explains Azure AD Connect directory synchronization for hybrid identity, including powerful on-prem and cloud service accounts and password-hash replication secrets.

Credential extraction

Using AADInternals on a compromised Connect server, he demonstrates extracting stored sync credentials from the local database and reusing them remotely when protections are weak—a common real-world gap.

Reverse engineering the sync protocol

Research uses Fiddler man-in-the-middle on Connect's SOAP plus binary XML traffic. He fixed a missing dictionary entry in an existing Fiddler plugin, enabling readable messages. Connect can CRUD synchronized cloud objects keyed by immutable ID or cloud anchor.

Bug bounty war stories

He previews two abuse chains against the sync API, including vendor fixes and his evasions, tied to substantial bug bounty payouts beyond his day job.

talks.title: #RomHack2022 - Davide TheZero - Security in a Immutable web3 World: Breaching Smart Contracts
talks.teaser: Reviews #RomHack2022 - Davide TheZero - Security in a Immutable web3 World: Breaching Smart Contracts and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Web3 security primer

Davide TheZero of Shielder walks from blockchain basics through smart-contract exploitation without ICO hype. Solidity compiles to EVM bytecode; ABI metadata defines contract interfaces similar to Swagger or symbol files for reversers. Execution requests broadcast to the network mutate on-chain state.

Immutable code, upgradeable reality

Deployed contracts are immutable, yet proxy patterns delegate calls to implementation contracts owners can swap via upgrade functions. This preserves user-facing addresses while changing behavior—creating trust and audit challenges when owners can redirect logic.

Web2 skills transfer

The talk bridges web2 researchers into web3 by covering EVM semantics, common vulnerability classes, and root-cause analysis of major historical breaches. Closing remarks stress that "immutable" blockchains still host mutable trust assumptions through admin keys, oracles, and upgradeable proxies.
